citations.review_text: Amazing art style. Can't wait to learn more about the world. I can tell this is a popular game for a reason.

I want to start off by saying that personally, I didn't like the game. The reason why I'm giving it a recommendation is because objectively speaking I think the game deserves it's praise. It definitely creates the feeling of urgency and danger when it comes to avoiding obstacles and finding shelter before the rain.
Apart from that, visually the game looks phenomenal: The artstyle is very unique and both playable characters and enemies look fantastic.

So, why didn't I like this game?
For me, the controls felt way too disorganized and movement felt increadibly frustrating; Very Janky and the throwing mechanics were weird. Apart from that, many elements of the game that are random (such as enemy locations or behaviour, at least from what i've experiences) are increadibly hard to deal with at times. You could have an area with no enemies where you can travel it freely, and then another area where you have a bazilion load of enemies that's pretty much impossible to get through. 
As a fan of difficult games, platformers in particular, I don't mind when the game doesn't hold your hand. That being said, in my opinion, there is a fine line between frustrating and difficult, and the game for me was more frustrating then it was difficult, which is why I stopped playing.

Returning to my initial point - The game itself is good, and I think that platformer fans or those that enjoy difficult games should give it a try. I personally don't like the game but this is my opinion, which isn't something that's universaly true to everyone. I'd still reccommand that you get the game on sale.

Maybe one day I'll return to it to give it another go, but for now I think I'll play something else.
A very fun and unique take on a metroidvania where you must forage for supplies to hibernate. I love the designs of the characters and the atmosphere is great, cant wait to play more.
One of the most interesting and engaging games. The fantastic atmosphere and music make it impossible to tear yourself away.

I trusted the user reviews but it seems this game has a fanbase akin to Silksong, so I was misled.

You won't read past this point so I'll make this short: it feels like a rage game, having no positive feedback for the player and making it a frustrating slog that only feels rewarding once you're done to cope with sunk cost.

I like challenging games, but people insisting you have to spend 5+ hours before you "get it" does not compel me to keep trying (that's what a tutorial is for). Or saying you have to "research" movement tech that the game doesn't outright teach you (so why try it?). Or insisting that it's a "simulation" of an ecosystem, but I don't know of any real-life ecosystem that respawns you in your bed when you die and reverses time. There's "difficult" and then there's calling brute force a playstyle. Some people might like spending 8 hours on the same room, but I'm not 20 anymore. Or 30, for that matter.

The concept and art style are nice. It's a shame that so many indie games have such a striking presence but the gameplay itself is so unsuited to the average player. I know through mods or 'remixing' things can be made easier, but that also feels like it goes against the developer's original intent, potentially cheapening the experience.

You won't read this far, but I kept my playtime low because I intend to get a refund. I assessed that I'm not the game's target audience and didn't waste any more time.

**This review is not me asking for advice. I don't care. I'm not playing it again. Comments are left on for people who want to discuss my review or ask questions, not tell me to "give it a chance".**

The world, art, sound design, music, and entire concept are all very well executed and engaging. The movement tech is also interesting, albeit something you have to investigate for yourself with zero suggestion that it might be there.

However, in a game primarily about getting from point A to B without dying, there are some real problems with the execution. More often than not, I find that I'm fighting against the world seed more than the actual enemies. Either a room spawns with nothing in it and I walk through without issue, or five lizards are camping the exact passageway I need to get into. Having a vulnerable protagonist is fine, but to give the player zero tools to deal with enemies that are just hanging out in death traps is very frustrating to deal with. Furthermore, there's no consistency in the creature behavior. The same motions that will cause a creature to rush straight at you on one cycle will elicit zero response from the same creature on a different cycle.

I understand why some people like this game, but the difficulty was not consistent and it made the overall experience pretty bad.

citations.review_text:
If you enjoy games like Hollow Knight, Silksong, and Dead Cells, you'll more than likely enjoy this. Beautiful art style, unique map system, gorgeous soundtrack, and overall interesting take on the natural cycle of life, death, and rebirth. 

That being said. Rain World does NOT hold your hand, it bites it off if you're not careful. You'll be constantly looking for food while simultaneously BEING the food. You get only the barest hints as to where you're supposed to go next, and RNG will not be on your side every time as you traverse the map, so you'll need to think fast and find different ways to your destination if you don't want to end up as some nasty beastie's lunch. The wiki will take up permanent residence in your web browser the more you progress, and once you hit the climax and reach the end, you'll be looking at the credits thinking to yourself 'drugs, not even once'. 

But each time you die, you learn. citations.review_text: Beautiful game, but very hard and often frustrating, and a bit long. Some features of the gameplay are frustrating. Enemies on a different screen can see you, but you can't see them. Sometimes your guide will warn you, but otherwise there is no way to see them. I've often walked to the next screen and right into the jaws of a lizard. The controls for movement are very inconsistent. Sometimes the little guy jumps, sometimes he just flops down to his death even though he's positioned properly and I hold the jump button for several seconds. The tail of the little guy serves no purpose - I know people have done a bunch of studies on the movement of the character and how to use the tail to do various things, but I've found it to hinder movement more than anything else. He folds himself in half in tunnels even if he goes into tunnels head first, he can't climb walls like a real slug, it maybe helps him jump but back legs should be strong enough to jump without the weight of the tail. Long story short, slug cat is far inferior to all other characters in the game and should be extinct. Then there's the lore... supposedly you can bring pearls to Looks to the Moon but ain't no way I'm going all the way back there, and there are only so many (5-8) bonus teleportations after completing achievements so not sure what the point is. The ending was a bit disappointing (may as well not go there and just continue playing; you get to the same "ending" by getting chomped, lol), but the journey was very interesting. I wish slug cat developed perks as it grew into adulthood, but it just stays as a relatively helpless baby slug cat. BUT - it's a really good game and it really immerses you into feeling like a little animal trying to stay alive and not get eaten. You can tell developers put in a lot of work on it. citations.review_text:
Highly recommend this game for people who like uncovering the past, getting good at overcoming new challenges and figuring things out by themselves. It was a lot of fun getting good at surviving each cycle.

My biggest downside with the game is that it's never going to explicitly tell you what to do past the tutorial. For me it was a wonderful experience due to that, but some players may not like that or feel lost and quit.

9.5/10

It's an unique platforming survival game that tests your wits and forces to learn how to survive in a mysterious world where most of what you will encounter tries to eat or kill you.

The game is probably difficult to get into because the first few hours as a new player are very rough and purposefully unguided. You're being thrown into the world, with little to no idea what you're doing, let alone what you're supposed to do. Dying is an inevitable part of the game, and especially at starts it takes time to realize that dying is part of the learning experience.

But after some time, you start getting used to the peculiar movement and keybinds, you forget less the game loop priorities, and the unfairness of being near the bottom of the food chain doesn't weight as nearly much on you as it did. You start to survive. That's when you may start to enjoy exploring, discovering and seeing the world interact with you and with itself.

And while 'progressing' in the game is made to throw you off very often, setting new challenges types that may seem impassable, know that there are multiple solutions, sometimes through, sometimes around. The key is to experiment with the world around you. Your character doesn't get stronger, doesn't learn new tricks. You have to learn them yourself in order to truly progress.

Movement is incredibly complex and full of quirks. You only really need 5-10% of it to navigate the whole game relatively easily. The rest can be useful, but is a bonus that can help you, not a requirement.

Graphically i think that the game world is very pretty, with great use of colors for scenery. My favorite part of the visuals are the creature design, which are procedural, making them feel very organic, lively and unpredictable.

Sound-wise, the sound design is right on point, and the soundtrack is excellent. The use of layering for threat themes (played during tense encounters) very dynamically conveys the urgency of these situation, acting as an additionna…

Now that i have 100 hours of experience i can say.
This is a MASTERPIECE of a game, the art, the lore, the mechanics, i love it.
BUT, the game is not meant for everyone, its very punishing, with alot of backtracking and sometimes situations that seem very unfair. Also the game gives near-zero clues on how to progress.
And so i must say, if you like very difficult games, with lore you must find by yourself and complex movement mechanics this is your game, if on the contrary you like more lineal games with less difficulty and a more clear story (which is totally fine) then i cannot recommend it.
10/10

On peut penser que le pixel art n'est pas si beau mais j'ai jamais autant été bouche bée en face de certains panoramas dans un jeu, j'ai plusieurs fois poser la manette pour apprécier ce que je voyais. En plus d'avoir les musiques qui sont exceptionnelles et matchent extrêmement bien l'ambiance du jeu. Je viens de finir le premier dlc et ce jeu est fou. Il m'a convaincu sur tous les aspects. I bought this game expecting to be the main character.

Turns out I'm a protein bar.

Rain World is what happens when a nature documentary gains sentience and decides you personally deserve to lose. Every creature has hopes, dreams, ambitions, and an overwhelming desire to make sure you never reach the next shelter.

The game doesn't hold your hand. It doesn't even acknowledge you have hands.

Every time I thought I understood the ecosystem, the ecosystem laughed, spawned three new lizards, and introduced me to a bird the size of a small apartment.

The AI is genuinely incredible. Half the time predators are hunting each other. The other half they've formed a temporary committee dedicated to making my day worse.

Movement starts out feeling like you're controlling an overcaffeinated wet sock. Twenty hours later you're chaining backflips, spear throws, wall jumps, and pipe tech like you've been training under a slugcat sensei your whole life.

The rain itself deserves an Oscar. Nothing motivates efficient route planning quite like hearing the sky announce, "Your survival subscription has expired."

This game somehow makes finding a tiny hole to sleep in feel like defeating the final boss. Every successful cycle has the emotional payoff of paying off your mortgage.

Would I recommend it?

Absolutely.

Would I recommend it to my friends?

Only the ones I'm willing to lose.

Pros:
Incredible ecosystem.
Gorgeous world.
Some of the smartest creature AI I've ever seen.
Every victory feels earned.
The modding community is great.

Cons:
I am no longer at the top of the food chain.
My therapist now has to hear about lizards.
The local wildlife has my address.

Hours played: Enough to develop prey instincts.

10/10. This game taught me that "skill issue" is a fundamental law of nature.

Wow do I love this game. It's the type of game which you either never get into or it takes over your life. Throughout my 1000 hours of playing and replaying the game I've encountered a lot of unfairness within the game however that's just the charm of the game. The AI of the game is unpredictable in the best way. With the experience I have, I do often figure out what I did wrong if I died (although not always). If you can get away the issues and start embracing them the game all of a sudden becomes a beauty.

The game is most definitely best experienced blind however if you don't find that fun then you definitely can look up a map to help. Issue is there's never going to be a way to revert that and play blind once more. The DLCs are also fantastic but this review shall focus on the base game. Some of the rooms in this game are absolutely stunning and the lore is incredibly deep and I love analysing things with my friends even if the thing might not be that big.

Being a small critter in a big world you don't know is just a fantastic feeling and exploration is a great thing to do. Modding is fantastic as well with how easy it is and how many new regions and campaigns there are to find. The AI of creatures is incredibly unique with all of them being procedurally generated and just watching them do their own thing after I die is just entertaining with the shenanigans they get up to.

There's just so much to do in the game if you love the game whether it's trying to explore new areas, introducing new people to the game to discuss things as they're learning without spoiling them of the ability to explore themself. Or just in general the vibes the game produces. I heavily recommend the game if you can accept the fact you are definitely going to lose some minor progress at times with it barely being your fault.

Rain World is a 2D survival platformer where you're playing as the lowest of the food chain trying to survive a wildlife that has outlasted its cycle of life while making sense of a long lost world in ruin and your life in it.
It will not be easy.
You won't fully understand what you're doing at first.
You will get lost and die a lot by the most spine-chilling and cortisol-inducing creatures you have ever seen.
You WILL find it unfair.
